title: Assessment scope & runbook: SIEM export, RBAC v2 checks, and evidence automation
body:
Purpose and audience:
This runbook defines the scope, coordination steps, evidence export schema, RBAC v2 validation checklist, and remediation workflow for external and internal security assessments. Intended audience: security engineers, SRE, platform owners, solutions engineering, and the vendor/red team engagement lead.

Context and objectives:
- Primary objective: provide a repeatable, low-friction process to collect verifiable audit evidence for penetration tests and vulnerability assessments while minimizing production impact and preserving privacy.
- Secondary objective: validate RBAC v2 enforcement across APIs, admin consoles, and private deployments; ensure audit logs are exportable to SIEM in a consistent format for triage and forensic review.

Scope (what testers may and may not test):
- In-scope: authentication flows (SSO, API key), authorization boundaries (RBAC v2 roles, role bindings), audit log generation and retention, SIEM export pipelines (JSON/CEF output), telemetry of privilege escalations, and evidence packaging. Includes hosted API endpoints, console, and dedicated/private deployment connectors used by customers.
- Out-of-scope: production customer data exfiltration (tests must use synthetic tenants), physical datacenter access, and any destructive attacks that will cause prolonged outages without prior coordination.

Pre-engagement checklist (security team / solutions engineering):
1) Scoping call with vendor/red-team: confirm test windows, allowed test vectors, and blast radius. Note the contact names and on-call for each window.
2) Create a dedicated test tenant/namespace in staging and a mirrored set of logging pipelines to avoid mixing test evidence with live customer logs.
3) Generate ephemeral credentials for testers (API keys with specific role bindings) and log them into the evidence registry (do not use production admin keys).
4) Configure SIEM ingestion for test namespace: ensure an ingest stream name like "redwood-pt-<engagement-id>" is created and test events are flowing before the engagement.
5) Approvals: Legal, Privacy, and Trust review signed off (attach sign-off artifact to the engagement ticket).

RBAC v2 validation checklist (automated + manual steps):
- Inventory check (automated): export role definitions and role bindings for the target namespace. Required fields: role_id, permissions[], resource_scope, created_by, updated_at.
- Negative tests (manual + automated): attempt actions with lower-privilege roles to ensure 403 responses and no side-effects. Log each attempt with the tester id and expected/actual result.
- Privilege escalation detection: run an automated scanner to attempt lateral privilege changes (role binding creation, impersonation APIs). Any successful escalation must be treated as high severity.
- Admin console checks: exercise UI flows for role creation, role editing, and assignment; verify audit entries are generated for each change (see audit schema below).
- Guardrails: confirm that critical operations require two-person approval where configured; simulate one-step vs two-step flows to ensure enforcement.

Audit log schema (required fields for evidence exports):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC string
- event_id: UUID v4
- actor_id: string (user:email or service:identifier)
- actor_role: string (role id at time of event)
- action: string (e.g., "role.bind", "model.deploy", "auth.token.issue")
- resource_type: string (e.g., "model", "route", "tenant")
- resource_id: string
- outcome: string ("success" | "failure")
- outcome_reason: string (optional, short code or human text)
- request_id: string (correlate with API tracing)
- ip_address: string (IPv4/IPv6)
- user_agent: string (agent or sdk info)
- request_payload_summary: string (redacted; sensitive fields should be replaced with "<redacted>")
- response_summary: string (truncated to avoid PII)
- audit_version: string (e.g., "rbac-v2-2024-10")
- retention_tag: string ("pt-temp" | "production")
Notes: all fields MUST be present for SIEM exports; if a field is not applicable, set to empty string.

SIEM export formats and requirements:
- Primary export: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) over secure SCP/S3 or direct HTTPS push to the assessor’s ingest endpoint. Each NDJSON object must include the schema fields above. File naming convention: redwood-<engagement-id>-audit-YYYYMMDD-HHMM.ndjson.gz (gzip preferred).
- Alternate export (if requested): CEF-wrapped events with a mapping table attached; CEF must include timestamp, deviceSeverity (map outcome to severity), and extension fields that map to event_id, actor_id, actor_role, resource_type, resource_id, request_id.
- Evidence manifest: alongside each export include a manifest.json with top-level metadata: engagement_id, exporter_name, export_time, record_count, schema_version, checksum (SHA256), and pointer to raw logs stored in cold storage.

Evidence automation pipeline (recommended configuration):
1) Trigger: on test start, set environment variable ENGAGEMENT_ID and enable "pt-temporary-retention" in the audit router.
2) Collector: use the existing audit exporter microservice with a filter that routes events from the test namespace to an ephemeral S3 bucket with server-side encryption.
3) Packaging lambda: when export finished or at scheduled intervals, run an automation job to: validate schema (field presence + type), gzip and checksum files, generate manifest.json, and upload to an evidence bucket with restricted ACLs.
4) Notification: publish a signed notification to the engagement Slack channel and create an artifact on the Jira engagement ticket with pre-signed object URLs (expiry 72 hours).
5) Retention policy: mark all test-scope logs with retention_tag "pt-temp" and set lifecycle rule to auto-delete after 90 days unless explicitly extended by legal.

Operational run steps during an engagement (day-of):
- 48h before: run export smoke test to the assessor endpoint; confirm receipt.
- 2h before: rotate the ephemeral tester API keys and post new keys in the encrypted secrets store; record rotation event in audit logs.
- Start: enable verbose audit level for affected services for the duration of the test.
- During test: monitor SIEM ingest rate and latency; if ingestion falls behind, escalate to infra on-call.
- End: run final export job, package evidence, and deliver to assessor via the agreed channel.

Remediation & findings workflow (how we track and close issues):
1) Triage: security lead reviews raw evidence and generates a findings summary. Each finding must include: description, proof-of-concept (log snippets + event_ids), severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low), affected scopes, suggested remediation, estimated effort, and a recommended owner.
2) Ticketing: create a JIRA ticket with component tags (e.g., api, console, audit, rbac). Use the template: Summary: "[PT][<engagement-id>] <short-desc>". Link the evidence manifest and sample ndjson lines.
3) Fix & test: owners implement remediation in a non-prod environment, run regression tests, produce before/after audit exports to demonstrate closure.
4) Verification: security lead verifies the fix, attaches verification exports to the ticket, and marks the ticket Resolved.
5) Postmortem and lessons learned: summarize recurring failure modes and update the RBAC v2 design page and audit-schema definitions.

Severity mapping (suggested):
- Critical: direct privilege escalation or ability to exfiltrate sensitive customer data from production.
- High: authorization bypass allowing privileged operations in staging or customer-facing control planes.
- Medium: missing audit entries for important actions or delayed log delivery to SIEM > 60 minutes.
- Low: logging format issues, schema field omissions (non-critical), or documentation gaps.

Sample finding (example text to include in tickets):
- Title: "Unauthenticated role-binding creation via internal API proxy"
- Summary: "The internal admin-proxy incorrectly forwarded X-User headers causing role-binding creation when requests were proxied from unauthenticated origins."
- Proof: include ndjson lines: {"timestamp":"2025-01-18T13:22:11Z", "event_id":"f3a2...", "action":"role.bind", "actor_id":"service:internal-proxy", "actor_role":"proxy-service", "outcome":"success"} (redacted)
- Remediation: patch proxy to validate auth header, add additional server-side enforcement in RBAC layer, and add unit/integration tests.
- Owner: platform-api team; ETA: 2 wks; Severity: High.

Post-engagement deliverables:
- Findings summary document (high-level exec summary + technical appendices).
- Raw evidence bundle (ndjson.gz + manifest.json + checksums).
- Verification exports for any closed issues.
- Runbook updates: update this document with any process or schema changes.

Appendix A: Quick automation scripts (pseudocode)
- Export validation (bash/pseudocode):
  for f in /tmp/exports/*.ndjson.gz; do gzip -d -c "$f" | head -n 5 | jq '{timestamp,event_id,actor_id,action,resource_type,resource_id,outcome,request_id}'; done
- Schema check (python pseudocode):
  required = ["timestamp","event_id","actor_id","actor_role","action","resource_type","resource_id","outcome","request_id"]
  for line in ndjson: obj = json.loads(line); missing = [r for r in required if r not in obj or obj[r] == ""]; if missing: emit error

Appendix B: Who to call (rotation):
- Security lead (on-call): Aisha Malik (pager: sec-oncall)
- Platform API owner: Ben Carter (slack: @benc)
- Observability / SIEM: Lina Zhou (slack: @linaz)
